hero.name: Shaikh Aryan Bilal
hero.lede: Backend-focused Software Engineer with 6+ years of experience in PHP, Laravel, WordPress, and Strapi, and familiar with Next.js for front-end development. I build scalable APIs, secure backend systems, and headless CMS solutions, with a growing interest in generative AI and AI-assisted workflows.

highlights: Backend-first engineering with PHP, Laravel, and WordPress
Headless & API-driven content delivery for web and mobile
Security by default — OWASP-aligned from logic to deployment
about: I've spent the last 6+ years as a backend-focused web engineer, mostly working with PHP, Laravel, and WordPress, with REST APIs and MySQL tying everything together. I like solving the harder, less visible problems around architecture, speed, and security that make an application actually work well once real users and real traffic show up.

Most of my work involves building custom backend systems: APIs, admin panels, WordPress plugins, and full application setups designed to grow without breaking. Lately I've also been working with Strapi, using it to build headless CMS backends that send content to websites, apps, and anything else that needs it. I try to keep the code clean and easy to understand, so someone else, or future me, can work with it later without trouble.

I'm not only backend, though. I know enough HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and jQuery to work across the stack when a project needs it, and I'm also familiar with Next.js, which is useful when pairing a headless CMS like Strapi with a modern front end. It makes working with front-end developers easier too.

Security is something I think about from the start, not at the end. I follow OWASP best practices and build with common risks in mind, like SQL injection, XSS, and CSRF, so the application stays safe from the ground up.

Outside of client work, I've been learning more about generative AI, trying to figure out where AI-based tools and automation actually make sense inside a web application, instead of just adding them because it's trendy.

If you're looking for someone who takes backend work seriously, can work across Laravel, WordPress, and Strapi, and cares about both security and long-term stability, let's connect. I'm always happy to share ideas, learn from other engineers, or help figure out a tough backend problem.
